name: Classes of Agentic AI Systems
description: Taxonomy of agentic AI system classes and concrete examples. Sources: Nowaczyk 2025 (5 families), Liu 2024 (18 patterns), Wang 2024 (survey), Moralles 2026 (SLR). Two node types: classes (categories) and concrete examples.

agentic-ai.name: Agentic AI Systems
agentic-ai.description: Systems that autonomously pursue goals by deciding what to do next, selecting and using tools, consulting and updating memory, and interacting with their environment under constraints (Nowaczyk 2025).

conversational-assistants.name: Conversational Assistants
conversational-assistants.description: Single-agent systems that interact via dialogue. Human-in-the-loop for every output. Primarily text generation with optional tool use. Low autonomy — the human reads and judges every response.

ex-claude-code.name: Claude Code
ex-claude-code.description: Anthropic's CLI agent. Reads code, proposes edits, runs commands. Human approves each action. Conversational interface with tool use.

ex-chatgpt.name: ChatGPT
ex-chatgpt.description: OpenAI's conversational assistant. Dialogue-based, can use tools (browsing, code interpreter, DALL-E). Human reviews all output.

ex-github-copilot.name: GitHub Copilot
ex-github-copilot.description: Code completion and chat assistant embedded in IDEs. Suggests code inline. Human accepts or rejects each suggestion.

task-automation-agents.name: Task Automation Agents
task-automation-agents.description: Single-agent systems that plan and execute multi-step workflows with reduced human oversight. Broader tool access. Medium autonomy — human sets the goal, agent executes.

ex-autogpt.name: AutoGPT
ex-autogpt.description: Autonomous agent that decomposes goals into tasks, executes them, and self-reflects. Uses Tree-of-Thoughts for multi-path planning. Minimal human intervention during execution.

ex-devin.name: Devin
ex-devin.description: Autonomous software engineering agent. Takes a task description, plans implementation, writes code, runs tests, debugs. Operates in a full development environment.

ex-voyager.name: Voyager
ex-voyager.description: Autonomous Minecraft agent. Explores, acquires skills, builds a reusable skill library. Plans and executes without human guidance. Continuous learning via episodic memory.

domain-specific-agents.name: Domain-Specific Agents
domain-specific-agents.description: Custom-built agents for specific professional or safety-critical environments. Tightly constrained tool access, domain-specific memory, formal verification. High autonomy within narrow scope.

ex-fleet-diagnosis.name: Fleet Diagnosis Agent (Nowaczyk)
ex-fleet-diagnosis.description: Agent monitoring autonomous electric vehicle fleets. Triages anomalies, runs digital-twin simulations, recommends mitigations within safety envelope. Goal Manager, Planner, Verifier, Safety Supervisor architecture.

ex-chemcrow.name: ChemCrow
ex-chemcrow.description: Chemistry research agent. Plans and executes multi-step chemical reasoning using specialised chemistry tools (reaction prediction, molecular property calculation).

ex-clinical-decision.name: Clinical Decision Support Agent
ex-clinical-decision.description: Healthcare agent that interprets patient data, suggests diagnoses and treatments. Operates under strict regulatory constraints (FDA, HIPAA). Requires audit trails and human override.

multi-agent-systems.name: Multi-Agent Systems
multi-agent-systems.description: Multiple specialised agents coordinating via protocols. Division of labour, negotiation, debate. Three topologies: supervisor-worker, peer collaboration, role-play. High autonomy — agents coordinate autonomously.

ex-metagpt.name: MetaGPT
ex-metagpt.description: Multi-agent software development. Agents play roles: architect, project manager, programmer, tester. Follow standardised operating procedures. Role-based cooperation pattern.

ex-crewai.name: crewAI
ex-crewai.description: Multi-agent orchestration framework. Agents grouped for discussion on topics. Supports debate-based cooperation, role assignment, and tool sharing.

ex-autogen.name: AutoGen
ex-autogen.description: Microsoft's multi-agent conversation framework. Treats conversation as computation. Programs agent roles, message routes, tool access, stop conditions. Supervisor-worker and peer patterns.

ex-generative-agents.name: Generative Agents (Stanford)
ex-generative-agents.description: 25 agents in a virtual town simulating daily life. Episodic memory, reflection, planning. Agents form relationships, spread information, coordinate activities autonomously.

embodied-agents.name: Embodied / Physical Agents
embodied-agents.description: Agents that act in the physical world via robots or autonomous vehicles. Actions have irreversible consequences. Require simulation-before-actuation, safety envelopes, human-in-the-loop for high-impact actions. Very high autonomy.

ex-inner-monologue.name: Inner Monologue
ex-inner-monologue.description: Robotic agent that decomposes instructions into actionable steps using LLM reasoning. Leverages human feedback for object recognition. Embodied reasoning through planning with language models.

ex-autonomous-vehicles.name: Autonomous Vehicle Systems
ex-autonomous-vehicles.description: Self-driving systems with perception, planning and actuation. LLM-augmented planning layers for complex scenarios. Safety-critical — requires certified monitors, geofences, kill-switches.

ex-smart-llm.name: SMART-LLM
ex-smart-llm.description: Multi-agent robot task planning using LLMs. Decomposes complex tasks into sub-tasks assigned to different robot agents. Coordination via shared plans.

web-agents.name: Web Agents
web-agents.description: Agents that interact with websites, APIs and GUIs. Volatile, untrusted environments. DOM changes, adversarial content, third-party scripts. Require sandboxing, deterministic contracts, data-not-instructions for untrusted text.

ex-webshop.name: WebShop
ex-webshop.description: Agent that navigates e-commerce websites to find and purchase products matching user specifications. Evaluated on product search and retrieval benchmarks.

ex-webarena.name: WebArena
ex-webarena.description: Benchmark for web agents across multiple website domains. Tests end-to-end task completion accuracy. Agents must navigate realistic web environments.

ex-apple-intelligence.name: Apple Intelligence
ex-apple-intelligence.description: Cross-application agent. Writing, image generation, schedule management across apps. Captures entities from photos, creates emoji. Agent adapter pattern across diverse tool interfaces.

simulation-agents.name: Simulation Agents
simulation-agents.description: Agents that simulate human behaviour, social dynamics, or complex systems. Used for research, training, and prediction. Must balance simulation fidelity with LLM knowledge boundaries.

ex-agentsims.name: AgentSims
ex-agentsims.description: Framework for evaluating LLM agents. Flexibly design planning, memory and action strategies. Measure effectiveness in interactive environments.

ex-social-simulacra.name: Social Simulacra
ex-social-simulacra.description: Simulated social community prototyping. Generates personas and social interactions to help designers understand community dynamics before building real platforms.
